text:
Sam Steel has gone eight games without a point, and three points in 16 games is a long way from last season's 33 in 73. He missed a game earlier this month for personal reasons, per CBS Sports and RotoBaller, and returned on Nov. 7. Beyond that, the season has just been quiet.

Some of it is luck. Dallas has scored 5.1 fewer goals than its chances with him on the ice, and he's shooting 6.7% where he usually sits around 13. But this drought isn't only bounces: his own chance rate is down from 0.65 expected goals per 60 to 0.48, and the Stars are four and a half points worse in shot share with him than without. Fewer chances and worse finishing on them is how you get a stretch like this.

The useful version of Steel is a third-line center who kills penalties and attacks off the rush; Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 55% of his shots coming in transition last season, and Evolving-Hockey had him at 1.1 wins above replacement. He's still on 16 minutes a night. Watch whether the chances come back before the minutes start to go.
